title: Omada Fusion Gateway 2.5G Ecosystem and Software Overview
author: Rohit Kumar
text:

Omada Fusion Gateway 2.5G Rear Angled 1
Omada has a new gateway device, and it is not what we were expecting. The Omada Fusion Gateway 2.5G is the company’s take on a business gateway device, launching with a different management experience. Instead of managing this device at an individual device level, it is much more of an integrated management experience with a local subscription-free controller. It is a 2.5GbE device on every port, making it a better fit for more modern WAN connections in the 1-2Gbps range.

Omada sent us not just this gateway, but also a PoE+ switch, a few APs, and mounting options for everything. The idea was that we would be able to test this as a solution rather than just as an individual device. We have to say this is sponsored. We will have more details on the individual devices soon, but we wanted to give folks a sense of what the solution looks like because I had no idea before testing these. Instead of doing a full deep-dive in subsequent pieces, I thought we could just have a guide to reference later.
If you want to buy these, you can check out the Omada store, or here are some Amazon affiliate links: Omada Fusion Gateway 2.5G, Omada 2.5GbE and 10GbE Switch, Omada EAP775-Wall, Omada EAP775-Outdoor, Omada EAP772 Indoor.
Omada Fusion Gateway 2.5G
The Omada Fusion Gateway 2.5G is a compact device with a surprisingly nice little color touchscreen on the front that can help you view diagnostic data.
Omada Fusion Gateway 2.5G Front 2
On the rear, we have a USB Type-C port and five 2.5GbE ports.
Omada Fusion Gateway 2.5G Rear Angled 1
You can set up the device via a Bluetooth app, or just log in at 192.168.188.1, the default gateway IP. To be fair, this is much less painful a setup than something like a Fortinet or a SonicWall, but a part of me would also love to have had a console interface as an option. I think this is designed for ease of use, but not much serial console automation as a design direction.
Omada Fusion Gateway 2.5G Setup 1
Once you get done with the setup, you have a nice GUI and dashboard. If you have used something like Ubiquiti UniFi, then this is going to be a comparable GUI. Both have unique features, and a bit more on how they do things, but that is the ease-of-use experience that Omada is targeting.
Omada Fusion Gateway 2.5G Dashboard
Here you can set up VPN access and manage different types of VPNs. There are even options on the WAN side to set up multi-WAN, so you could have, like, a VPN on a WAN link, or have a backup 5G or Starlink WAN along with a wired ISP. There are a lot of options there.
Omada Fusion Gateway 2.5G Setup VPN Server
You can set up a WLAN in the settings, as well as configure guest networks, change the radio frequencies used, and so forth. The idea behind the gateway is that it integrates a local controller, so you can set up the wireless on the controller, and then it will cascade the configuration to Wi-Fi APs.
Omada Fusion Gateway 2.5G STH Omada WLAN Setup
Here is a look at the LAN side with a nice little topology chart.
Omada Fusion Gateway 2.5G LAN Topology
You can set up IDS/IPS, content blocking, and more here as well. We will do this when we run this through our Keysight CyPerf setup.
Omada Fusion Gateway 2.5G Setup IDS IPS
There is a list of clients with information, including their connections.
Omada Fusion Gateway 2.5G Clients
We found a few other neat tools, like a console migration, for when you may need to upgrade the unit. Having a backup/ rescore feature is fairly common, but an actual migration assistant is a neat function. We did not get to test this, but it is there in the UI.
Omada Fusion Gateway 2.5G Controller Migration
There are also a number of fairly standard network tools so you can ping from devices, do packet capture and such.
Omada Fusion Gateway 2.5G Network Tools
Perhaps one of the big powers of this is that you can use other Omada devices and manage them from the controller. This is the reason we got a big box from Omada, because the gateway by itself feels like it needs Wi-Fi APs, and a PoE+ switch to power those APs. If you were to ask why you might want to use this over other solutions, the ability to centrally manage VLANs, WLANs, guest networks, and so forth is a huge time saver. There are quite a few folks out there running small-to-medium businesses who have relied on maybe an ISP router/Wi-Fi combo, or perhaps that plus an individual AP. Moving to a centrally managed solution is an enormous upgrade in ease of use.
Omada Fusion Gateway 2.5G Devices
Next, let us get to rackmount and magnetic mounting options, and then to the 2.5GbE/ 10GbE PoE+ switch.
